Project: Django. Upgrade being assessed: 3.2 -> 4.2.
This change was introduced in release 4.1. Source: Django 4.1 release notes (official_release_notes). Section: Django 4.1 release notes / Backwards incompatible changes in 4.1 / Database backend API.
Version facts from package metadata for this release (authoritative for version numbers): [
 {
  "release": "4.1",

 }
]

ITEM:
<<<
Several date and time methods on DatabaseOperations now take sql and params arguments instead of field_name and return 2-tuple containing some SQL and the parameters to be interpolated into that SQL. The changed methods have these new signatures: * DatabaseOperations.date_extract_sql(lookup_type, sql, params) * DatabaseOperations.datetime_extract_sql(lookup_type, sql, params, tzname) * DatabaseOperations.time_extract_sql(lookup_type, sql, params) * DatabaseOperations.date_trunc_sql(lookup_type, sql, params, tzname=None) * DatabaseOperations.datetime_trunc_sql(self, lookup_type, sql, params, tzname) * DatabaseOperations.time_trunc_sql(lookup_type, sql, params, tzname=None) * DatabaseOperations.datetime_cast_date_sql(sql, params, tzname) * DatabaseOperations.datetime_cast_time_sql(sql, params, tzname)
>>>

PARENT CONTEXT (same section, for disambiguation only):
<<<
Django 4.1 release notes / Backwards incompatible changes in 4.1 / Database backend API: This section describes changes that may be needed in third-party database backends. BaseDatabaseFeatures.has_case_insensitive_like is changed from True to False to reflect the behavior of most databases. DatabaseIntrospection.get_key_columns() is removed. Use DatabaseIntrospection.get_relations() instead. DatabaseOperations.ignore_conflicts_suffix_sql() method is replaced by DatabaseOperations.on_conflict_suffix_sql() that accepts the fields, on_conflict, update_fields, and unique_fields arguments. The ignore_conflicts argument of the DatabaseOperations.insert_statement() method is replaced by on_conflict that accepts django.db.models.constants.OnConflict. DatabaseOperations._convert_field_to_tz() is replaced by DatabaseOperations._convert_sql_to_tz() that accepts the sql, params, and tzname arguments. Several date and time methods on DatabaseOperations now take sql and params arguments instead of field_name and return 2-tuple containing some SQL and the parameters to be interpolated into that SQL. The changed methods have these new signatures: * DatabaseOperations.date_extract_sql(lookup_type, sql, params) * DatabaseOperations.datetime_extract_sql(lookup_type, sql, params, tzname) * DatabaseOperations.time_extract_sql(lookup_type, sql, params) * DatabaseOperations.date_trunc_sql(lookup_type, sql, params, tzname=None) * DatabaseOperations.datetime_trunc_sql(self, lookup_type, sql, params, tzname) * DatabaseOperations.time_trunc_sql(lookup_type, sql, params, tzname=None) * DatabaseOperations.datetime_cast_date_sql(sql, params, tzname) * DatabaseOperations.datetime_cast_time_sql(sql, params, tzname)
>>>

Decide the disposition:
- "risk": the item describes something that can break an app/deployment, require migration work, or create operational risk.
- "context": it is accurate but needs no action at 4.2 (no user action required, deprecated-but-working, additive feature). Give the reason.

For "risk", produce one or more risk paths. Use separate paths for separate symbols/APIs when they can be checked independently. Hard rules:
1. Every condition has at least one quote copied EXACTLY, character for character, from ITEM or PARENT CONTEXT (contiguous span, 3-40 words, no ellipses, no added words). Do not fix typos or formatting.
2. Each path has exactly one condition with category "version" stating that the upgrade crosses release 4.1 (quote the text that ties the change to this release, or the change statement itself), and at least one application/deployment condition (category api_usage, configuration, dependency, runtime, deployment, database, behavior or test_coverage) describing what the app or deployment must use/have for the risk to apply.
3. If the text does not state something you need, do not assert it: use role "uncertain" and explain in ambiguities. derived_by: "extraction" when the text states the fact; for an application/deployment condition ("the application uses X"), use "extraction" when the text names X as the thing affected by the change. Use "inference" only when you infer an affected symbol, scope or impact that the text does not name. Only add ambiguities for real gaps or conflicts in the text, not for the general fact that a specific application has not been inspected.
4. role: "required" (must hold), "alternative" (any one of the alternatives suffices), "optional" (raises impact), "disqualifying" (if it holds, the risk does NOT apply, e.g. not using the new opt-in API), "uncertain".
5. operator/expected_value must be checkable: e.g. operator "present" with expected_value the literal symbol; "less_than" with a version; "equals" with a setting value. expected_value is a string.
6. If a replacement API/setting/version is named, put the migration step in suggested_actions and add a condition for any behavior that differs in the replacement when the text states one.
7. search_queries: for app-side conditions with a literal symbol, give ripgrep regexes (tool "ripgrep"), kubectl commands (tool "kubectl") or SQL (tool "sql") that would find usage. Empty list if no literal symbol.
8. primary_symbol: the most specific identifier of the change (full apiVersion string like "policy/v1beta1", setting name, function, flag, or runtime name like "Python"/"Node.js"). symbols: all identifiers involved.
9. risk_level rubric: critical = upgrade fails or data is at risk for most users meeting the conditions (e.g. unsupported runtime/database version, removed API version that stops serving); high = code or config meeting the conditions breaks at upgrade; medium = behavior change or migration with a clear workaround; low = edge case, cosmetic, or warning-only.
10. fires_at: "upgrade" (at upgrade time), "first_use" (when a feature is first exercised), "rotation" (on credential/password rotation), "rollout" (on deployment rollout), "future_removal" (deprecated now, removed later).
11. applies_to: fill upgrade_method (e.g. "pg_upgrade", "dump/restore"), cluster_type, or from_versions (a version specifier like "<3.1") ONLY if the text restricts applicability; otherwise null.
Do not output confidence.

paths.path_name: Third-party database backend overrides date/time DatabaseOperations methods with old field_name signatures
paths.description: In Django 4.1, several date and time methods on DatabaseOperations take sql and params arguments instead of field_name and return a 2-tuple of SQL and parameters. Third-party database backends (or custom code) that define or call these methods with the old signature or return a single SQL string need updating.

conditions.statement: The upgrade crosses release 4.1, where these DatabaseOperations methods changed signature and return value.
quotes: Several date and time methods on DatabaseOperations now take sql and params arguments instead of field_name
conditions.relevance: Ties the signature change to release 4.1, which is crossed when upgrading from 3.2 to 4.2.

conditions.statement: The project contains or uses a custom or third-party database backend whose DatabaseOperations overrides or calls the changed date/time methods.
quotes: This section describes changes that may be needed in third-party database backends.
conditions.relevance: The section is about third-party database backends; those defining or calling these methods must adopt the new signatures and 2-tuple return.
ambiguities: The text does not state whether code outside a database backend that calls these methods directly is affected.

conditions.statement: The project uses only Django's built-in database backends and does not override or call these methods.
quotes: This section describes changes that may be needed in third-party database backends.
conditions.relevance: The section scopes the change to third-party database backends, so projects not touching these methods are not affected.

suggested_actions: Update overridden methods to the new signatures: date_extract_sql(lookup_type, sql, params), datetime_extract_sql(lookup_type, sql, params, tzname), time_extract_sql(lookup_type, sql, params), date_trunc_sql(lookup_type, sql, params, tzname=None), datetime_trunc_sql(lookup_type, sql, params, tzname), time_trunc_sql(lookup_type, sql, params, tzname=None), datetime_cast_date_sql(sql, params, tzname), datetime_cast_time_sql(sql, params, tzname).
Change the methods to return a 2-tuple of SQL and the parameters to be interpolated into that SQL.
Update any callers of these methods to pass sql and params and to handle the tuple return value.
Check that the third-party database backend in use supports Django 4.2.
